JUDGMENT The present appeal is filed by the appellant/claimant challenging the judgment and award dated 16.04.2015 in MVC.No.2323/2014 passed by the XIX Additional Small Cause Judge and MACT,
Bengaluru, for seeking enhancement of compensation.

XIX Additional Small Cause Judge and MACT,
Bengaluru

sentences.text:
2. Brief facts of the case are as under:
On 15.10.2013 at about 10.30 p.m., the claimant was traveling in an Indica car bearing registration No.KA- 10-3468 near 12th Main Junction, 100 Feet Road,
Indiranagar.
At that time a tempo bearing registration No. KA-54-3006 came with a high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the car, due to which the claimant sustained injuries.

He was immediately taken to CMH Hospital,
Indiranagar.
Thereafter he was taken to Hosmat Hospital wherein he took treatment.
3. The claim petition was filed by the appellant/claimant seeking compensation.

The Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition and awarded compensation of Rs.1,51,024/- with interest at 6%
Sri. Anthony Bernard vs Sri. Thimmegowda on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64779190/
2 p.a., from the date of petition till the date of realization. Being aggrieved by the same, the present appeal is filed before this Court.

4. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the materials on record.
5.

The Tribunal has granted compensation under various heads as follows:
a) Towards pain and agony Rs. 20,000.00 b) Towards medical expenses Rs. 7,864.00 C) Towards loss of income Rs. 18,000.00 d) Towards disability Rs. 92,160.00 e) Towards food and nourishment Rs. 10,000.00 f) Towards attendant Rs. 3,000.00
In the present case, from the medical evidence on record including the doctor's evidence, it is proved that the claimant had suffered fracture of left humerus.
The claimant is stated to be a computer operator.
the Tribunal has awarded Rs.20,000/- towards pain and agony.
Considering the nature of injury sustained, the same is enhanced to Rs.40,000/-.
7. Rs.7,864/- is granted by the Tribunal towards medical expenses and the same is kept in tact.
8. The Tribunal has taken the notional income at Rs.6,000/- per month which is on a lesser side.
The accident is of the year 2013 and therefore income of Rs.8,000/- per month is to be taken into consideration as recognized by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.

Therefore, loss of income during the laid up period for three months will come to Rs.24,000/- (Rs.8,000/- x 3).
9.
The claimant had suffered fracture of shaft of left humerus.
The doctor has deposed that the claimant has suffered disability of 23% to the left upper limb and for the whole body at 8%.

Considering the fact that functional disability is not a mathematical formula, on the basis of nature of injuries, the nature of avocation, functional disability is to be assessed as per the judgment of the Supreme Court in Rajkumar vs Ajay Kumar and Another [(2011) 1 SCC 343].

entities.text: Rajkumar vs Ajay Kumar and Another [(2011) 1 SCC 343]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Accordingly, 10%
functional disability is to be taken into consideration.
As the claimant was aged 32 years on the date of accident, the appropriate multiplier is '16'.

Therefore, loss of future income due to disability is reassessed at Rs.1,53,600/-: -
Rs.8,000/- x 10% x 16 x 12 = Rs.1,53,600/-
10.
The Tribunal has awarded Rs.10,000/- towards food and nourishment and Rs.3,000/- towards attendant charges.
The same are on lesser side.
Therefore, compensation of Rs.25,000/- is awarded towards food, nourishment, attendant charges, etc.,
Further, a sum of Rs.12,000/- is awarded for future medical expenses.

sentences.text:
Thus, in all the appellant/claimant is entitled to the compensation as follows:
a) Towards pain and agony Rs. 40,000.00 b) Towards medical expenses Rs. 7,864.00 C) Towards loss of income Rs. 24,000.00 d) Towards disability Rs. 1,53,600.00 e) Towards food and nourishment Rs. 25,000.00 and attendant f) Towards future medical expenses Rs. 12,000 Total Rs. 2,62,464.00 12.
The Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.1,51,024/-, but the appellant/claimant is entitled to total compensation of Rs.2,62,464/-.
Hence, the appellant is entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs. 1,11,440/- (Rs.2,62,464/- - Rs.1,51,024/-).

Therefore, the appellant/claimant is entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.1,11,440/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization.
13.
In the present case, the Tribunal has fastened the liability on the owner of the tempo on the ground that the driver of the tempo was not having driving lience.
The charge sheet was also filed against the driver of tempo.
Hence, it proves that the driver of the tempo was not having driving licence to drive the tempo.
Hence, the insurance company has established the defence under section 149 (2) of the Motor Vehicles Act.

Therefore, as per sub-sections (1), (4) and (7) of section 149 of the Motor Vehicles Act, the insurance company shall satisfy the claim amount to the claimant who is third party at first instance, then recover from the owner of tempo bearing registration No.
KA-54-3006 as per the principles laid down by the Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Swaran Singh And Others [(2004) 3 SCC 297], Pappu and Others vs Vinod Kumar Lamba and Another [(2018) 3 SCC 208] and also of this court in the case of New India Assurance Company Limited vs. Yellavva And Another [2020 ACJ 2560 (HCK)].
14.
